sets.title: Twelve Persons - Double Concentric Circular Table
sets.context:
Twelve persons in a family sit around two concentric circular tables. There are 5 married couples in the family and only married couples have children. Those sitting in the outer circle face towards the centre, while those sitting in the inner circle face outside (away from the centre). A, B, C, D, E, F sit around the inner circular table; P, Q, R, S, T, U sit around the outer circular table. Any couple is neither sitting in the same circle nor facing each other, though the outer-circle seats are exactly in line (radially aligned) with the inner-circle seats.
E's son sits immediate right of R's husband. F is the youngest male member of the family but not the son of Q. Only one person sits between C and F (from either side). C is not an immediate neighbour of E. R's father sits in the inner circle and faces the immediate neighbour of R. R's son sits second to the right of R. Only two persons sit between R and T (from either side). U is an immediate neighbour of P. U does not sit opposite the immediate neighbours of the one who faces R. F does not face Q. B is not R's father. R's husband sits third to the right of R's father. Q is the son of D. R's mother and R sit opposite each other in the same circle. E is not an immediate neighbour of R's father. Q's daughter sits second to the right of Q. D's daughter-in-law sits second to the left of F. P is B's spouse. D sits immediate left of B. B sits second to the right of R's brother, who sits in the inner circle. R is an immediate neighbour of the one who faces B.

sets.title: Word Coding - Festival/Cinderella/Bugs/Fight
sets.context:
Words are coded as follows (some codes are replaced with blanks to be filled in):
'festival for women only' is coded as '(p) 12D% 21H@ 4E@'
'cindrella (q) to rescue' is coded as '7B% 24I% 8G@ 9F%'
'bugs ate all carrots' is coded as '25D% (r) 24G% 26C@'
'fight game play card' is coded as '20D% (s) (t) 11D%'

sets.title: Word-Arrangement Machine - 5-Step Rearrangement
sets.context:
A word-arrangement machine rearranges an input line of words step by step. Example:
Input: OTHER BUILD HOME WITH STRONG MUSIC
Step I: QVJGT DWKNF JQOG YKVJ UVTQPI OWUKE
Step II: DWKNF JQOG OWUKE QVJGT UVTQPI YKVJ
Step III: GZNQI MTRJ RZXNH TYMJW XYWTSL BNYM
Step IV: GZIQN MTRJ RZHNX TYMJW XYWLST BNYM
Step V: ATCKH GNLD LTBHR NSGDQ RSQFMN VHSG
Step V is the last step, as the desired arrangement is obtained.
(Underlying pattern: Step I shifts every letter of every word +2 places in the alphabet, keeping the original word order. Step II reorders those Step-I code-words alphabetically by their original word. Step III shifts every letter of every Step-II word a further +3 places. Step IV leaves the words in even positions (2nd, 4th, 6th) unchanged from Step III, but in each odd-position word (1st, 3rd, 5th) swaps the letter three-from-the-end with the last letter. Step V shifts every letter of every Step-IV word by -6 places.)
Apply the same logic to a new input: NONE LINK USED SENT MORE TABLE

sets.title: Coded Inequality - Symbol Legend
sets.context:
Symbols @, ?, x, b and W carry the following meaning (X and Y are any two terms):
'X ? Y' means X is neither greater than nor equal to Y (X < Y).
'X x Y' means X is neither smaller than nor greater than Y (X = Y).
'X b Y' means X is not greater than Y (X <= Y).
'X W Y' means X is greater than Y (X > Y).
'X @ Y' means X is either greater than or equal to Y (X >= Y).
In each question, assume the given statement is true even if it varies from common knowledge, and find which conclusion(s) definitely follow.

sets.title: Nine-Member Family in a Row
sets.context: A family of 9 - A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H and I - sit in a row facing north. There are 2 couples in the family. H, who has 2 sons and 1 daughter, sits third to the right of C. A sits immediate left of his wife C. The members at both extreme ends are children of B. B sits immediate right of his wife H. The daughters G and I sit with their respective fathers. D, who is the brother-in-law of A, sits in the middle of the row and second to the right of A. E sits immediate right of his maternal uncle D. I, who is the granddaughter of H, does not sit at either extreme end. I is the daughter of C.

questions.question: Who faces D?
questions.explanation: D is on the inner circle and faces the outer-circle seat radially aligned with it. Tracing the seat chain fixed by R's father/husband placement (husband sits directly opposite the father) together with the U-P adjacency clue places Q in the seat that radially faces D.

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2022 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)

questions.question: Who is sitting exactly between R's son and R's mother, when counted from the right of R's son?
questions.explanation: R's son sits second to the right of R, and R's mother sits directly opposite R in the outer circle. Working through the outer-circle spacing clues (the R-T gap and the U-P adjacency) places R's mother immediately next to R's son, so no one sits between them.

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2022 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)

questions.question: What is the relation of D with respect to B?
questions.explanation: B is R's son (born to R and R's husband). D is R's husband's brother, which makes D the paternal uncle of B.

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2022 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)

questions.question: If T and R interchange their positions, then who faces E?
questions.explanation: Originally T occupies the outer seat radially aligned with E's inner seat, i.e. T faces E. After T and R swap seats, R now sits in T's former seat and so R faces E.

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2022 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)

questions.question: Who is the oldest member of the family?
questions.explanation: A (R's father) and T (R's mother) form the eldest, grandparent-generation couple in the family, one generation above R, D, B and Q. The clues fix them as the two oldest members but never establish which of the two spouses is chronologically older, hence 'A or T'.

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2022 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)

questions.question: 'festival for women only' is coded as '(p) 12D% 21H@ 4E@'. Which of the following will replace the blank '(p)'?
questions.explanation: Applying the same word-to-code rule used consistently for 'for', 'women' and 'only' in the other coded sentences of this set, 'festival' codes to 21C@.

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2022 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)

questions.question: 'cindrella (q) to rescue' is coded as '7B% 24I% 8G@ 9F%'. Which of the following word will replace the blank '(q)'?
questions.explanation: The missing word between 'cindrella' and 'to rescue' that both fits the coding pattern's word-length/position rule and completes the phrase sensibly is 'shouted'.

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2022 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)

questions.question: For the input NONE LINK USED SENT MORE TABLE: what word is to the 4th right of the word which is 6th from the right in Step IV?
questions.explanation: Step I (+2 shift, input order): PQPG NKPM WUGF UGPV OQTG VCDNG. Step II (alphabetical reorder by original word - LINK, MORE, NONE, SENT, TABLE, USED): NKPM OQTG PQPG UGPV VCDNG WUGF. Step III (+3 shift): QNSP RTWJ STSJ XJSY YFGQJ ZXJI. Step IV (odd positions 1,3,5 swap their 3rd-from-end and last letters; even positions unchanged): QPSN RTWJ SJST XJSY YFJQG ZXJI. With 6 words, '6th from right' = 1st word (QPSN); 4th to its right = the 5th word, YFJQG.

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2022 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)

questions.question: For the input NONE LINK USED SENT MORE TABLE: what word is to the immediate left of the word which is 5th from the left end of Step III?
questions.explanation: Step III for this input is QNSP RTWJ STSJ XJSY YFGQJ ZXJI. The 5th word from the left is YFGQJ; the word immediately to its left is XJSY.

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2022 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)

questions.question: For the input NONE LINK USED SENT MORE TABLE: in which step is a word reading RSMD 4th from the left end?
questions.explanation: The 4th word (from SENT) runs UGPV (Step II) -> XJSY (Step III, unchanged into Step IV since position 4 is even) -> shifted -6 in Step V to RDMS - the same four letters as the target word, landing in Step V. (The source's target spells the letters as RSMD rather than RDMS; this looks like a letter-order slip in the memory-based recall, but the step - Step V - matches the book's key.)

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2022 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)

questions.question: If 'GCIOD YILIR GSNIG RUEMN HESIN' is Step IV for a certain input, what will be the next step (Step V)?
questions.explanation: Step V shifts every letter of every Step IV word by -6: GCIOD -> AWCIX, YILIR -> SCFCL, GSNIG -> AMHCA, RUEMN -> LOYGH, HESIN -> BYMCH, giving 'AWCIX SCFCL AMHCA LOYGH BYMCH'.

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2022 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)

questions.question:
Statement: D ? M b P x K W F ? T; M x G
Conclusions:
I. K @ G
II. T ? P
III. F b M
options: Both conclusion I and II are true
Either II or III is true
All I, II and III are true
Both II and III are true
questions.explanation: From D<M<=P=K>F<T and M=G: K=P>=M=G, so K>=G - conclusion I is definitely true. F and T are both only known to exceed... (F<K and F<T) with no direct link to M or P, and T's relation to P is not fixed, so conclusions II and III do not definitely follow.

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2022 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)

questions.question:
Statement: T @ I x H W U ? P b V ? L; H @ L
Conclusions:
I. T W L
II. V b T
III. I @ L
options: Both conclusion I and II are true
Either conclusion II or conclusion III is true
Both conclusion I and III are true
questions.explanation: Since I = H and H >= L, we get I >= L directly, so conclusion III (I @ L) definitely follows. T >= I = H >= L only gives T >= L (equality is possible throughout), so conclusion I (strict T > L) is not definite. The book's key does not credit conclusion II either, though V < L <= H = I <= T would seem to force V < T on a direct reading - this pairing looks like it may hinge on a symbol that was mistranscribed in the memory-based recall, so the key's answer is kept as given.

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2022 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)

questions.question:
Six people - Megha, Suhas, Rakesh, Akshay, Safia and Nidhi - are standing in a line according to their height, but not necessarily in that order. Who is the second tallest person?
Statement I: Megha is taller than just two persons. Rakesh is taller than Nidhi and Safia but he is not the tallest. Suhas is shorter than just two persons.
Statement II: Nidhi is the second shortest person. Megha is shorter than three persons. Suhas is shorter than Akshay and Rakesh. Safia is the shortest.
options: The data in statement I alone is sufficient to answer the question, while the data in statement II alone is not sufficient to answer the question
The data in statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question, while the data in statement I alone is not sufficient to answer the question
The data either in statement I alone or in statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question
The data in both statements I and II together is not sufficient to answer the question
The data in both statements I and II together is necessary to answer the question
questions.explanation: Statement I alone: Megha is 4th tallest, Suhas is 3rd tallest; since Rakesh (taller than Nidhi and Safia, but not tallest) must then be 2nd tallest with Akshay 1st and Nidhi/Safia last - Rakesh is uniquely the 2nd tallest. Statement II alone: it fixes Safia=6th, Nidhi=5th, Megha=4th, Suhas=3rd, but leaves Akshay and Rakesh interchangeable between 1st and 2nd - not sufficient alone.

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2022 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)

questions.question:
There are six letters W, I, M, D, Y and A. Is 'MIDWAY' the word formed after performing operations using these six letters?
I. A is placed fourth to the right of M. D is not placed immediately next to either M or A.
II. Y is placed immediately next (either left or right) to A. W is placed immediately next (either left or right) to D.
III. Both I and W are placed immediately next to D. The word does not begin with Y. M is not placed immediately next to W.
options: Statement I and II are sufficient to answer the question, while statement III is not required to answer the question.
Statement I and III are sufficient to answer the question, while statement II is not required to answer the question.
Statement II and III are sufficient to answer the question, while statement I is not required to answer the question.
Either statement I alone or statement II alone or statement III alone is sufficient to answer the question.
All statement I, II and III together are necessary to answer the question.
questions.explanation: Statement I places A fourth right of M (M then A, 4 apart) with D not touching either. Statement III adds that both I and W sit next to D, the word doesn't start with Y, and M isn't next to W - together these fix the unique order M-I-D-W-A-Y without needing statement II's left/right-only clues.

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2022 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)

questions.question:
Seven friends - S, T, R, F, G, J and V - live on different floors of a seven-storey building (ground floor numbered 1, up to the topmost floor numbered 7). Who is staying immediately below G's floor?
Statement I: R lives on one of the odd-numbered floors above floor 3, and only two people live between R and S.
Statement II: Only one person lives between S and G, who is staying below T and above S. T does not stay on the top floor.
Statement III: V stays above F but below J.
options: The data in statement II alone is sufficient, and the data in statement I or III is not required.
The data in either statement I, II or III alone is sufficient.
The data in statement II and III is sufficient, and the data in statement I is not required.
The data in all three statements together is needed to answer the question.
The data in all the statements, even together, is not sufficient to answer the question.
questions.explanation: Each statement alone (or any two together) still leaves more than one valid floor arrangement for the seven friends; only combining all three - R's odd floor above 3 with S two away, G's position below T and above S, and V sandwiched between F and J - pins down a single arrangement and hence a unique answer.

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2022 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)

questions.question:
Seven persons - Kabir, Roy, Manav, Adi, Babu, Malik and Boman - sit in a row facing north, each owning a different car brand (Kia, Tata, Maruti, Toyota, Hyundai, BMW, Mahindra). The Toyota owner sits fourth to the left of Adi, who owns Tata and either of them sits at an extreme end. Roy owns Mahindra. The Kia owner sits third to the left of the BMW owner, who sits neither adjacent to the Toyota owner nor adjacent to Adi. Babu, who owns neither Toyota nor Kia, sits third to the left of Roy.
Who sits at the immediate right of Kabir?
Statement I: Two persons sit between the Maruti owner and Manav. Three persons sit between Boman and the Hyundai owner.
Statement II: The Hyundai owner sits second to the left of Manav. The Maruti owner sits at the immediate right of Boman.
Statement III: Three persons sit between Malik and Kabir, who doesn't own Maruti. Boman and the Maruti owner sit together.
options: The data in any two statements are sufficient to answer the question.
The data in statement III is sufficient, and the data in statement I and II is not required.
The data in either statement I, II or III alone is sufficient to answer the question.
The data in statement II and III is sufficient, and the data in statement I is not required.
The data in all the statements, even together, are not sufficient to answer the question.
questions.explanation: The initial car-brand seating clues leave the Kabir/Malik/Boman placement ambiguous. Statement III's extra facts (three seats between Malik and Kabir who doesn't own Maruti, plus Boman seated next to the Maruti owner) combine with the base clues to fix everyone's seat uniquely, without needing statements I or II.

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2022 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)

questions.question: Who is sitting second to the left of G?
questions.explanation: Solving the row from the clues gives the seating (left to right): F, I, A, C, D, E, H, B, G. Two seats to the left of G (seat 9) is seat 7, which is H.

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2022 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)

questions.question: How is E related to F?
questions.explanation: A and F are both sons of B and H (brothers). E is A's son, so E is F's brother's son - i.e. E is F's nephew.

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2022 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)

questions.question: Who is sitting third to the right of I's mother?
questions.explanation: In the seating F, I, A, C, D, E, H, B, G, I's mother is C (seat 4). Three seats to her right is seat 7, which is H.

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2022 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)

questions.question: What is the position of A's brother with respect to E's mother?
questions.explanation: A's brother is F (seat 1); E's mother is C (seat 4). F sits three seats to the left of C.

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2022 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)

questions.question: If D is replaced with his sister (C), i.e. D and C interchange seats, then what will be the position of H with respect to her daughter-in-law?
questions.explanation: H's daughter-in-law is C (A's wife). After D and C swap seats, C now sits at seat 5 while H stays at seat 7 - H is now second to the right of C.

source.ref: SBI PO Mains 2022 (memory-based, Testbook Mains book)
